children.name: Archaefructus liaoningensis Sun et al., 1998
children.description: Archaefructus is an extinct genus of herbaceous aquatic seed plants with three known species. Fossil material assigned to this genus originates from the Yixian Formation in northeastern China, originally dated as late Jurassic but now understood to be approximately 125 million years old, or early Cretaceous in age.

children.name: Archaefructus sinensis Sun et al., 2002
children.description: An extinct herbaceous aquatic angiosperm known from compression fossils in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, northeastern China (~125 Ma). Described in 2002, it was the more complete specimen founding the basal-angiosperm family Archaefructaceae, preserving roots, a rhizome, finely dissected leaves, and elongate reproductive axes bearing paired stamens and helically arranged conduplicate carpels. Its form prompted interpretation as a possible sister to all other flowering plants.
